annotation_description: Playing Forest instead of Fabled Passage on turn 1 is suboptimal. Fabled Passage should be played first because: (1) It can fetch a Forest, giving the same G mana access for Sazh's Chocobo on turn 2. (2) Playing Fabled Passage T1 and cracking it gets a tapped basic, which is fine since there's nothing to cast T1 anyway. (3) On turn 2, playing Forest as the land drop gives two untapped lands for Badgermole Cub or Sazh's Chocobo. (4) More importantly, with Sazh's Chocobo and Mossborn Hydra in hand, Fabled Passage's sacrifice trigger counts as a landfall trigger, enabling extra counters. Playing Passage T1 and the natural Forest T2 yields two landfall triggers on T2 (if Passage is cracked then), which is better with landfall creatures. (5) With Icetill Explorer allowing lands from graveyard, having Fabled Passage in the graveyard earlier could matter. The sequencing with Fabled Passage first is strictly better here.

Playing Riverpyre Verge turn 1 instead of Steam Vents means no blue mana is available this turn (Verge only produces {U} if you control an Island or Mountain). This means Spell Pierce and Spell Snare cannot be held up on the opponent's turn 2, missing the chance to counter key early plays like Badgermole Cub or other 2-mana threats. The opponent already has Sazh's Chocobo and will likely make an important turn 2 play.

Casting Burst Lightning before playing a land this turn. With Riverpyre Verge in hand, they should play it first, then cast Burst Lightning using Riverpyre Verge's red mana, keeping Steam Vents untapped to hold up Spell Pierce or Spell Snare on the opponent's turn 2.

Sazh's Chocobo is a 0/1 that grows with each landfall trigger. Left unchecked, it will quickly become a serious threat. Burst Lightning kills it cleanly right now. Going face for 2 damage on turn 2 is nearly meaningless — the opponent is at 20 life and this isn't an aggro deck (it's a UR control/tempo deck with Eddymurk Crab and counterspells). Meanwhile, the Chocobo will accumulate +1/+1 counters every turn as the green opponent plays lands, potentially becoming a 3/4 or larger creature that Burst Lightning can no longer handle.

Playing Fabled Passage on turn 2 with only 2 total lands means the fetched land enters tapped (fewer than 4 lands), leaving only 1 untapped mana and preventing casting Badgermole Cub this turn. Additionally, Fabled Passage is more valuable later when 4+ lands are controlled (fetched land enters untapped). While Passage does give 2 landfall triggers for Chocobo vs 1, missing the Badgermole Cub deployment is a bigger tempo loss.

The player chose to cast Burst Lightning (presumably targeting the opponent or a creature) instead of playing a land. They have Riverpyre Verge in hand and only one land on the battlefield (Steam Vents, which is tapped). Missing this land drop is very costly - they're stuck on one land in a deck that needs to develop mana to cast Eddymurk Crab and other spells. Additionally, with only one tapped land, they likely can't even cast Burst Lightning this turn since Steam Vents is tapped and they have no untapped mana sources. Even if they could cast it, playing a land first is strictly better sequencing since Riverpyre Verge enters untapped (they control two or fewer other lands... wait, Riverpyre Verge always enters untapped as it has no ETB tapped condition). Playing the land would let them hold up Spell Snare or Spell Pierce next turn.

Sazh's Chocobo is a 1/2 (started as 0/1, got one +1/+1 counter from landfall) and will continue to grow with each land drop. Burst Lightning deals exactly 2 damage, which would kill the Chocobo cleanly. Instead, sending 2 damage to the face of an 18-life opponent is negligible pressure, especially for a blue-red deck that appears to be more of a tempo/control deck (Spell Pierce, Spell Snare, Eddymurk Crab in hand). The Chocobo will continue accumulating +1/+1 counters every turn and become a serious threat that will be much harder to remove later. Additionally, the opponent has Earthbender Ascension and other green ramp cards that could accelerate land drops, making the Chocobo grow even faster.

Playing the land before casting Badgermole Cub means the Chocobo gets a +1/+1 counter from the land's landfall trigger, but Badgermole Cub's earthbend ability (which animates a land and puts a +1/+1 counter on it) would also trigger landfall if sequenced differently. More importantly, casting Badgermole Cub first (with the 2 forests already available) and then playing the land would trigger landfall on both Sazh's Chocobo AND the earthbent land creature (if it counts as entering). However, the key issue is that playing the Forest first is actually fine for Chocobo, but casting Badgermole Cub before the land drop would let you earthbend the newly played Forest after it enters untapped (since you'd play it post-Cub). Actually, with 2 Forests untapped, casting Badgermole Cub first uses both forests, then playing the 3rd Forest gives landfall to Chocobo. Playing Forest first gives landfall to Chocobo, then casting Cub with 2 of 3 forests uses mana but earthbends a land. The sequencing matters because playing the land first and then casting Badgermole Cub means the Cub's earthbend targets one of 3 forests. If instead they cast Cub first (2 forests, both tapped), then play Forest (landfall on Chocobo), the earthbend from Cub still targets one of the 2 tapped forests. The land-first line is slightly better since it gives an extra untapped forest as an earthbend target, but the real consideration is whether Mossborn Hydra at 3 mana (with the 3rd forest) would have been better than Badgermole Cub - Mossborn Hydra enters as 1/1 with trample, and subsequent land drops double its counters, which could be very powerful. But Badgermole Cub at 2 mana plus land drop is reasonable. The sequencing of land before creature is slightly suboptimal in that it telegraphs information, but functionally the play is acceptable.

With 3 Forests available and a Fabled Passage in the graveyard, Earthbender Ascension would have been a stronger play. It costs {2}{G} (same as Mossborn Hydra), but it earthbends 2 lands (creating two 1/1 creature-lands with haste) AND fetches a basic land to the battlefield. This would provide immediate board presence comparable to the Hydra (two 1/1s vs one 1/1), plus ramp for next turn to cast Icetill Explorer, and start accumulating quest counters for the landfall trigger. The Mossborn Hydra enters as a 1/1 with trample, and while its landfall ability to double counters is powerful, Earthbender Ascension sets up the mana base and board state more effectively at this stage. Additionally, playing Earthbender Ascension first means future land drops (including from Icetill Explorer next turn) would trigger both the Ascension's quest counters and the Hydra's counter-doubling when the Hydra is cast later with more lands available.

Casting a second Mossborn Hydra (which enters as a 0/0 with one +1/+1 counter, making it a 1/1) is suboptimal when Earthbender Ascension would earthbend 2 lands into creatures, fetch a basic land (triggering landfall on both Hydras and Sazh's Chocobo), and start accumulating quest counters. The Ascension line generates far more value: earthbending 2 lands creates two 1/1 hasty creatures, the fetched land triggers landfall doubling the existing Hydra's counters (1→2→4 with the second land entering), grows Sazh's Chocobo, and sets up future landfall triggers to be even more explosive. The second Hydra starting as a 1/1 is much less impactful.
